title: Independent musl qualification scope review
head: ff72d462d74f9eb856aa9edbc368caad9c466708
conclusion: Current blocking GNU-labelled and musl-labelled Linux test jobs use the same GNU/glibc RBE platform. Independent current-source musl V8 dependency artifacts exist, but their smoke steps explicitly skip. No reviewed receipt qualifies current Rust/Hepta product execution under musl.

full_decoded_log.basis: ci_audit retained complete decoded original job log including terminal cleanup
ci_audit retained complete decoded original job log including terminal cleanup

current_blocking_jobs.evidence_owner: ci_audit independently retains the two complete original logs; this review independently read fixed workflow/action/wrapper/platform sources.
current_blocking_jobs.classification: Two matrix jobs and cache namespaces; one Linux libc target class, not two independent libc runtime qualifications.

source_evidence.meaning: Both Linux CI labels select ci-linux, whose target platform is //:rbe.
Root rbe alias resolves to generated @rbe_platform.
Generated execution/target platform declares Linux and libc gnu.2.28 with a pinned Ubuntu-based RBE container.

Matrix labels enter setup target input; no Linux musl --platforms override is supplied by the test command. Verify-release covers debug_assertions-off compilation under the same default Linux CI platform.
Target input is documented as cache namespacing.
Linux wrapper chooses ci-linux and appends that config.

Registers LLVM and rules_rs toolchain sets and includes both musl triples in Cargo dependency metadata. Metadata availability and broad registration are not evidence that a Rust musl product test executed.
Existing manual platform_data transitions target @llvm//platforms:linux_amd64_musl and linux_arm64_musl.
Existing codex and hepta calls instantiate explicit musl product build targets.
V8 explicitly selects musl target platforms; Cargo smoke excludes all musl targets and exits successfully after a skip message.
Existing full-CI compile/lint matrix includes explicit musl targets; existing Linux runtime-test callers select GNU targets only.
Reusable nextest flow builds an explicit target archive and executes the archive; its current Linux callers are GNU, not musl.
Tag-only release workflow has genuine Cargo --target musl product build steps, with existing tool setup, V8 checksums, and prehashed bwrap packaging.
Existing musl linker/build preparation is available for a future qualification; it was not installed or run by this review.
PR release-mode sweep uses first-party wildcard targets, not a recorded explicit invocation of the manual musl CLI transition.
Blocking workflow invokes bazel.yml and the smaller rust-ci.yml; full postmerge CI is a different workflow.
Postmerge flow, not this current PR, invokes rust-ci-full.

recommended_reporting.blocking_linux: Linux GNU/glibc RBE — GNU-labelled lane / musl-labelled lane
recommended_reporting.v8: musl-target V8 dependency build (cache-backed); Cargo smoke skipped
recommended_reporting.rust_musl_product_build: Not qualified by reviewed current-head receipts

recommended_reporting.limits: Toolchain registration, platform-triple dependency metadata, downloaded musl host tools, successful skip steps, and other-head release artifacts do not qualify current product runtime.

next_choices.action: Prepare a separate nonpublishing qualification using one existing explicit x86_64 musl CLI transition above. Retain GNU execution toolchains for proc macros/build tools, record resolved musl target and resulting product ELF/hash/source, and obtain an actual build result before broadening scope.
next_choices.why: Reuses existing registered platform/transition; no new platform definition or rewrite of the current blocking matrix is needed.
next_choices.remaining: No such build was started by this review; Rust target toolchain/linker resolution still needs real qualification.

next_choices.action: Execute those exact musl-linked product bytes and selected original behavioral tests, recording executable/ELF identity, OS/architecture, command, JUnit counts and all skips/retries. The existing explicit-target nextest archive workflow is a reusable mechanism only after validating musl prerequisites and a real musl caller.
next_choices.naming: A musl-linked process run on Ubuntu is a bounded musl runtime result, not Alpine deployment acceptance; full integration coverage must be separately named.
next_choices.remaining: Do not count --no-run, archive creation, staging or skip-exit-zero as runtime; do not remove capability/security oracles.

next_choices.action: Reuse the musl parts of rust-release build preparation (musl linker setup, checksum-verified V8 artifacts, bwrap build/finalize/hash, explicit cargo --target) in a separately reviewed nonrelease job if the Bazel product transition cannot qualify.
next_choices.limits: Do not trigger tag/release/signing or change dependencies to manufacture a passing label.

actions_taken: Read-only GitHub GETs and in-memory evidence composition. No builds, tool installation, platform definitions, matrix/filter/dependency edits, workflow starts/reruns, or ref changes.
